newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHORT RATES DROP, FORWARDS EASIER, BONDS FLAT.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHORT RATES DROP, FORWARDS EASIER, BONDS FLAT.

text.p: Greek interbank depos opened lower, particularly in very short periods, with increased liquidity, dealers said. Forex forwards were easier across-the-board.
Mark/drachma opened firmer, piercing the 157 level and ecu/drachma was easier. Bonds were little changed in thin trading volume.

"Short-term depos are down 20 basis points and rates in longer periods have eased 10 basis points in what appears to be better liquidity conditions," said a dealer at a private bank. "There are few deals so far and the market is quiet."
Bond prices were holding late Wednesday levels in the absence of trading incentives, bond dealers said.

"The market continues to be very quiet and prices are frozen," said a bond trader at a private bank. "I do not expect to see any price movement before the central bank cuts its 11.90 percent basic depo facility rate or its 14-day intervention rate."
The mark was quoted at 157.19/24 from Wednesday's 156.960 fix, the dollar at 277.27/37 drachmas from 276.640 and the ecu at 309.36/46 from 309.47 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma is trading around 309.35 after opening at 309.50 and mark/drachma pierced the 157 level on the back of its firmer tone against the French franc and the lira."
Ecu/drachma is directionless but biased downwards, the dealer said.
"All eyes are on sterling today with the market expecting the Bank of England to hike interest rates 25 to 50 basis points," the dealer said.
